mcqs.q: A PFM crown is best described as:
opts: Metal on the inside, covered with porcelain on the outside
Metal throughout, polished to look like enamel
A resin shell bonded to a metal post
mcqs.explain: The metal gives strength and the porcelain gives the natural appearance.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT another name for a PFM crown?
mcqs.explain: An all-ceramic crown contains no metal substructure at all.

mcqs.q: The metal coping of a PFM crown provides:
opts: The opacity that masks the dentine
mcqs.explain: It is a thin cast metal shell that fits the tooth.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of the opaque porcelain layer?
opts: To hide the grey colour of the metal
To build the final shape of the tooth
To bond the crown to the cement
mcqs.explain: It is the first thin porcelain layer applied over the coping.

mcqs.q: Which porcelain layer builds the shape and natural colour of the tooth?
mcqs.explain: Opaque masks the metal; body and incisal porcelain do the shaping and shading.

mcqs.q: The metal collar is a thin band of metal at the margin, usually placed:
opts: On the lingual side where it is not seen
On the labial side for strength
mcqs.explain: Putting it lingually keeps the grey metal out of sight.

mcqs.q: Which is an advantage of the PFM crown?
opts: It is strong enough to be used for bridges
It is the most conservative of all crowns
It is more esthetic than an all-ceramic crown
It never shows any metal at the gingival margin
mcqs.explain: The metal substructure resists fracture, which an all-ceramic crown cannot match for a span.

mcqs.q: Compared with a full metal crown, a PFM crown is:
mcqs.explain: The porcelain veneer is what makes it acceptable in a visible site.

mcqs.q: Which is a disadvantage of the PFM crown?
opts: It is not conservative — it removes a lot of tooth
It cannot be used as a bridge retainer
It has poor retention and resistance
It cannot be matched to tooth colour at all
mcqs.explain: The porcelain needs room, so considerable tooth structure must be removed.

mcqs.q: The metal of a PFM crown may become visible as:
opts: A grey line at the gum
A white opaque band at the incisal
A dark shadow on the radiograph only
A translucent halo at the margin
mcqs.explain: This is why it is less esthetic than an all-ceramic restoration.

mcqs.q: Why does placing the facial margin subgingivally increase risk?
opts: It increases the potential for periodontal disease
It prevents the porcelain from bonding
It reduces the retention of the crown
mcqs.explain: The margin is placed there to hide the metal, at a periodontal cost.

mcqs.q: A survey crown under a removable partial denture can be modified to incorporate:
opts: Occlusal and cingulum rests and milled guide planes
mcqs.explain: These features are milled into its metal substructure.

mcqs.q: Which is a contraindication to a PFM crown?
opts: A young patient with a large pulp chamber
A root-canal treated tooth needing coverage
A tooth to be used as a bridge retainer
A tooth with a large existing restoration
mcqs.explain: Deep reduction in a young tooth can expose the pulp.

mcqs.q: When esthetic demand is very high, which restoration is preferred?
opts: PFM with a labial metal collar
mcqs.explain: All-ceramic avoids the grey metal substructure entirely.

mcqs.q: Too little tooth reduction for a PFM results in:
opts: A bulky crown or a white, opaque look
A margin that cannot be located
mcqs.explain: Metal, opaque and body porcelain must all fit inside the original tooth contour.

mcqs.q: The recommended incisal reduction for an anterior PFM is:
mcqs.explain: That gives a strong, translucent porcelain edge.

mcqs.q: The recommended labial reduction for an anterior PFM is:
mcqs.explain: This leaves room for metal plus porcelain.

mcqs.q: The labial margin of an anterior PFM is prepared as a:
mcqs.explain: The shoulder gives porcelain its thickness at the margin.

mcqs.q: The lingual wall and margin of an anterior PFM are prepared as a:
mcqs.explain: Only metal sits lingually, so less depth is needed.

mcqs.q: The lingual concavity of an anterior PFM is reduced by about:
mcqs.explain: Enough to give clearance with the lower teeth.

mcqs.q: The total taper of the walls should be about:
mcqs.explain: Enough draw to seat, little enough to retain.

mcqs.q: The simple rule for finish lines in a PFM preparation is:
opts: Porcelain side deeper (shoulder), metal side shallower (chamfer)
Porcelain side shallower, metal side deeper
Both sides prepared as a 1 mm shoulder
Both sides prepared as a feather edge
mcqs.explain: The depth follows what material has to occupy the space.

mcqs.q: Reducing the labial surface in ONE plane along the incisal angle produces walls that are:
opts: Too tapered and close to the pulp
mcqs.explain: Following the incisal angle alone cuts towards the pulp.

mcqs.q: Reducing the labial surface in ONE plane along the long axis results in:
opts: No room at the incisal, giving a bulky crown
Excessive taper of the lingual wall
mcqs.explain: The tooth curves incisally, so a single long-axis plane leaves nothing removed there.

mcqs.q: In the correct TWO-plane labial reduction, the gingival part follows:
opts: The long axis of the tooth
The incisal curve of the tooth
The path of insertion of the bridge
mcqs.explain: The incisal part follows the tooth's curve, the gingival part the long axis.

mcqs.q: The labial shoulder continues onto the proximal surfaces and ends:
opts: A little lingual to the contact, blending into the lingual chamfer
On the lingual surface at the cingulum
mcqs.explain: The two finish lines must join smoothly.

mcqs.q: Which bur is used to cut the labial shoulder?
mcqs.explain: The flat end is what produces the 90° step.

mcqs.q: Which bur is used for the lingual concavity of an anterior tooth?
mcqs.explain: Its shape matches the concavity being cut.

mcqs.q: Which instrument is used for proximal reduction without damaging the neighbour?
mcqs.explain: A thin bur passes through the contact leaving a thin layer of enamel.

mcqs.q: The enamel hatchet is used to:
mcqs.explain: It is a hand instrument used during finishing.

mcqs.q: What should be prepared BEFORE starting the preparation?
opts: A putty (silicone) index of the tooth
mcqs.explain: The index is used later to check the reduction.

mcqs.q: What is the first step in the preparation sequence?
mcqs.explain: Guides are made first, then the tooth is removed one surface at a time.

mcqs.q: How many depth grooves are cut on the labial surface?
mcqs.explain: They are cut in two planes, a gingival half and an incisal half.

mcqs.q: The depth of the labial orientation grooves is about:
mcqs.explain: The bur's own width is used as the guide.

mcqs.q: During labial reduction, why is only one half removed at a time?
opts: The other half remains as a reference
mcqs.explain: Keeping a reference half makes it easy to see the depth and the two planes.

mcqs.q: In step 4, the lingual wall is made parallel to:
opts: The gingival part of the labial wall
The incisal part of the labial wall
The long axis of the adjacent tooth
mcqs.explain: It ends in a 0.5 mm chamfer.

mcqs.q: During proximal reduction, a thin layer of enamel is deliberately left to:
mcqs.explain: The thin layer is removed last, once access is safe.

mcqs.q: How is the finished preparation evaluated?
opts: The putty index is replaced and the space checked from every side
The provisional is cemented and reviewed
The shade tab is held against the tooth
mcqs.explain: The gap between index and tooth is the room available for the crown.

mcqs.q: For a posterior PFM, occlusal reduction where porcelain covers the cusp is:
mcqs.explain: Where it is metal only, 1.5 mm suffices.

mcqs.q: For a posterior PFM, occlusal reduction where the surface is metal only is:
mcqs.explain: Metal needs less thickness than metal plus porcelain.

mcqs.q: The functional cusp bevel is placed on which cusp?
opts: Buccal in the lower, palatal in the upper
Palatal in the lower, buccal in the upper
The non-supporting cusp of either arch
mcqs.explain: The supporting cusp is bevelled to give enough restorative thickness.

mcqs.q: On a posterior PFM, the buccal margin is prepared as a shoulder because:
opts: Porcelain is carried there, where it shows
The metal collar is thickest there
It is easier to access buccally
mcqs.explain: A lingual chamfer is used where only metal sits.

saqs.q: Define a PFM crown and name its parts.
saqs.a: A PFM crown is a full crown made of metal on the inside, covered with porcelain on the outside; the metal gives strength and the porcelain gives a natural, tooth-like look. Formally, it consists of a complete-coverage cast metal crown (or substructure) veneered with a layer of fused porcelain to mimic a natural tooth, and the extent of the veneer can vary. Its parts are: the METAL COPING, a thin cast metal shell that fits the tooth and gives the strength; the OPAQUE PORCELAIN, the first thin layer, which hides the grey colour of the metal; and the BODY AND INCISAL PORCELAIN, which build the shape and natural colour. The METAL COLLAR is a thin band of metal at the margin, usually on the lingual side where it is not seen. Other names: metal-ceramic crown, ceramo-metal crown, PFM.

ans.text: A full crown made of metal on the inside, covered with porcelain on the outside — the metal gives strength, the porcelain gives a natural, tooth-like look. Also called the metal-ceramic or ceramo-metal crown.

What it does
rows: a thin cast metal shell that fits the tooth — gives the strength
the first thin layer — hides the grey colour of the metal
builds the shape and the natural colour

ans.text: The metal collar is a thin band of metal at the margin, usually placed lingually, where it is not seen.

saqs.q: List the advantages and disadvantages of the PFM crown.
saqs.a: ADVANTAGES — strong, as the metal resists fracture, so it can be used for bridges; esthetic, looking like a natural tooth and much better than a full metal crown; and good retention and resistance, because it covers the whole tooth. DISADVANTAGES — not conservative, removing a lot of tooth structure; less esthetic than all-ceramic, as the metal can show as a grey line at the gum; the porcelain can chip; and gum health, because the labial margin is often placed below the gum for esthetics, which increases the potential for periodontal disease.

Disadvantages

Not conservative — removes a lot of tooth structure

Less esthetic than all-ceramic — the metal can show as a grey line at the gum
Good retention and resistance — covers the whole tooth
Gum health — the labial margin is often placed subgingivally, raising the potential for periodontal disease

saqs.q: Give the indications and contraindications for a PFM crown.
saqs.a: INDICATIONS — a tooth needing full coverage and esthetics (large filling, fracture, root-canal treated tooth); a retainer for a fixed dental prosthesis (bridge); a survey crown under a removable partial denture, which can be modified to incorporate occlusal and cingulum rests and milled proximal and reciprocal guide planes in its metal substructure; and teeth requiring complete coverage, as for a full metal crown. CONTRAINDICATIONS — young patients with large pulp chambers, because the deep reduction can expose the pulp; very high esthetic demand, where all-ceramic is better; and when a more conservative option can do the job.

list: A tooth needing full coverage AND esthetics — large filling, fracture, root-canal treated tooth
A retainer for a fixed dental prosthesis (bridge)
A survey crown under a removable partial denture — modified to carry occlusal and cingulum rests and milled proximal and reciprocal guide planes

head: Contraindication
Why
rows: the deep reduction can expose the pulp
no reason to remove more tooth than the job needs

saqs.q: Give the minimum reduction dimensions for an anterior PFM preparation.
saqs.a: INCISAL EDGE 2 mm, for a strong translucent porcelain edge. LABIAL SURFACE 1.2–1.5 mm, for room for metal plus porcelain. LABIAL MARGIN a shoulder 1 mm wide, for porcelain thickness at the margin. LINGUAL CONCAVITY about 1 mm, for clearance with the lower teeth. LINGUAL WALL AND MARGIN a chamfer of 0.5 mm, as there is metal only here. TAPER about 6 degrees total, for good retention with no undercuts. The simple rule is that the porcelain side is deeper (shoulder) and the metal side shallower (chamfer).

saqs.q: Why is the labial surface reduced in two planes?
saqs.a: If reduced in ONE plane along the incisal angle, the walls become too tapered and come close to the pulp. If reduced in ONE plane along the long axis, there is no room at the incisal and the crown is bulky. TWO planes is correct: the gingival part follows the long axis and the incisal part follows the curve of the tooth.

head: Result
rows: walls too tapered, coming close to the pulp
no room at the incisal → a bulky crown
correct — gingival part follows the long axis, incisal part follows the tooth curve

saqs.q: List the armamentarium for a metal-ceramic crown preparation.
saqs.a: Round-end tapered diamonds for depth grooves, axial walls and the lingual (deep) chamfer; a flat-ended tapered diamond for the shoulder preparation; a football- or wheel-shaped diamond for the lingual reduction of anterior teeth; a needle diamond for proximal reduction; flat-ended and round-end tapered finishing burs; and enamel hatchets. A putty (silicone) index of the tooth should also be made before starting, to check the reduction.

head: Instrument
Use
rows: depth grooves · axial walls · the lingual chamfer
proximal reduction without touching the next tooth

ans.text: Also prepare a putty (silicone) index of the tooth before you start — it is used to check the reduction.

saqs.q: Set out the seven steps of the preparation.
saqs.a: 1 Depth-orientation grooves — three grooves on the labial surface, in two planes, about 1.2–1.5 mm deep. 2 Incisal reduction — grooves 2 mm deep in the incisal edge, remove between them following the original shape, and check 2 mm clearance in all movements. 3 Labial reduction — remove between the grooves one half at a time keeping the two planes, forming a 1 mm shoulder that extends onto the proximal a little lingual to the contact. 4 Lingual reduction — the concavity about 1 mm with a football diamond, and the cingulum wall parallel to the gingival part of the labial wall, ending in a 0.5 mm chamfer. 5 Proximal reduction — a thin bur through the contact leaving a thin layer of enamel, joining the labial shoulder to the lingual chamfer at about 6 degrees taper. 6 Finishing — smooth all walls, round sharp angles, and make the shoulder smooth and flat. 7 Evaluation — replace the putty index and check the space from every side, the taper, the absence of undercuts and the clarity of the margins.

steps: Depth-orientation grooves — three on the labial, in two planes, 1.2–1.5 mm deep
Incisal reduction — grooves 2 mm deep, remove between them following the original shape; check 2 mm clearance in all movements
Labial reduction — one half at a time, keeping the two planes; form a 1 mm shoulder extending proximally, a little lingual to the contact
Lingual reduction — concavity ≈ 1 mm (football diamond); cingulum wall parallel to the gingival labial wall, ending in a 0.5 mm chamfer
Proximal reduction — thin bur through the contact, leaving a thin layer of enamel; join shoulder to chamfer at ≈ 6° taper
Finishing — smooth all walls, round sharp angles, make the shoulder smooth and flat
Evaluation — replace the putty index and check the space, the taper, the absence of undercuts and the margins

ans.text: Why this order — the guides are made first, then the tooth is removed one surface at a time, then it is smoothed and checked.

saqs.q: How does a posterior PFM preparation differ from an anterior one?
saqs.a: The same principles apply with a few differences. OCCLUSAL REDUCTION is 2 mm where porcelain covers the cusp and 1.5 mm where it is metal only. A FUNCTIONAL CUSP BEVEL is placed on the supporting cusp — buccal in the lower and palatal in the upper — to give enough thickness. And porcelain is placed where it shows: a buccal shoulder for porcelain, with a lingual chamfer where there is metal only.

buccal shoulder for porcelain · lingual chamfer where metal only

saqs.q: Summarise what a good PFM preparation shows.
saqs.a: 2 mm incisal clearance; 1.2–1.5 mm labial reduction in two planes; a smooth 1 mm labial shoulder; a 0.5 mm lingual chamfer; about 6 degrees taper with no undercuts; rounded line angles; clear continuous margins; and the neighbouring teeth untouched.
